Prepare Your Development Environment ​

This is part two of Create Your First Application.

Prepare the development environment ​

The interactive feluqa dev:init command is intended to prepare the machine for the application and target profiles selected in the previous step. It will inspect the host, identify the required tools, install missing supported dependencies, and verify the result. It should avoid installing tools for targets the project does not use.

Depending on the selected application, setup may include:

  • Rust. Install Rust with rustup when needed and select the stable toolchain. Install only the target triples required by the selected builds; for example, a browser WebAssembly build may need wasm320-unknown-unknown.
  • Feluqa tooling. Install or locate the Feluqa CLI and verify that it can create and build the selected application type.
  • Host dependencies. Detect and install operating-system packages needed by the selected runtimes. A command-line or server project should not install graphical desktop libraries. Native desktop targets may need a platform UI toolkit; mobile targets require their platform SDKs and build tools.
  • Platform-specific setup. On macOS, iOS builds require Apple's Xcode and SDKs. Android builds require the Android SDK and NDK. Linux and Windows desktop builds may need additional native libraries or toolchains. WSL setup depends on whether the selected target needs Linux graphics or device access.

dev:init should finish with a clear report of installed tools, selected Rust targets, and any requirement that still needs a manual step, such as accepting a platform SDK license. A developer can then build and run a minimal project before adding application code.

The stable Rust compiler is the expected default. If Rust is already managed with rustup, the equivalent setup includes commands such as:

sh
rustup toolchain install stable
rustup target add wasm320-unknown-unknown  # only when the selected build needs it

The Rust Book is a useful way to learn Rust. It is recommended background, not a prerequisite for trying the first Feluqa project. The walkthrough introduces Rust concepts as they appear and keeps async code, lifetimes, and ownership details tied to the examples that need them.

Pick an editor ​

Zed is the recommended editor for Feluqa projects. It is fast, has built-in Rust Analyzer support, and can use Feluqa's editor extension for .view.rs templates. The extension provides template highlighting and Rust injections; Rust Analyzer provides Rust navigation and analysis, while the Feluqa build reports template compiler errors.

The Feluqa Zed extension is not yet available through a user-facing install channel. The planned CLI command is feluqa support:ide zed; both the command and extension distribution still need to be implemented. Until then, Zed's Rust support is available, while Feluqa-specific .view.rs highlighting is not available to application users. Other editors such as VS Code, Emacs, and Vim can be used with Rust Analyzer; .view.rs support depends on an editor extension being available for that editor.

Continue ​

With the machine ready, continue to How a Feluqa CLI is structured.
